Hi Sam — great questions. Answers below and quick next steps.

Hosted API limits & scaling:
- Default trial: 10 req/s and 60k tokens/minute aggregate per org; per-request context up to 8k tokens for most models. These are conservative defaults to protect latency during public trial. (If you need higher we can bump this for the sandbox.)
- Paid plans: baseline is 50 req/s and 300k tokens/minute; we offer higher tiers and can set custom rate limits via a support request or during onboarding.
- Requesting increases: open a support ticket or we can route via your account rep (me) and our infra team typically responds within 24-48 hours for sandbox increases.

Dedicated vs Private quick notes:
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool, SLA-backed latency/uptime; minimum commit typically a monthly node reservation (we can provide pricing ranges). Sandbox provisioning ~3-7 business days depending on sizing.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full isolation and KMS control, used for regulated workloads. Provisioning timeline depends on network and ops; usually 2-6 weeks for VPC setup, longer for on-prem.

Data residency & retention:
- Hosted API supports region-aware endpoints (api.us.redwood.com, api.eu.redwood.com). You can pin your account to a region for data residency. Default request logs are retained 30 days; longer retention can be added as an enterprise add-on.

Quickstart curl (attached in the guide):
- curl -X POST https://api.us.redwood.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","prompt":"Say hi"}'

Attachments:
- redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (same as attached previously)
- redwood-sla-summary.pdf (baseline SLAs and Dedicated differences)

- If procurement wants pricing ranges, I can share a concise onepager.
